newsitem.title: USA: Miami man impersonated police to attract women.
newsitem.headline: Miami man impersonated police to attract women.

text.p: Abram Zayas hoped that dressing up as a policeman would attract women.

His impersonation was so good he once got a ride from two genuine Miami police officers and turned up at their station the next day to thank them. Now he is in a Dade County jail charged with impersonating a police officer, use of a firearm in a felony, grand theft and burglary.

Police spokesman Bill Schwartz said Zayas, 22, strolled around in a full police uniform and told detectives he wanted to impress women. "You know the old cliche that women love men in uniform? He was willing to break the law to test the theory," Schwartz said.
"I'd be interested to talk to his girlfriends to see if it worked. It hasn't for me," Schwartz added.

The charges related to the theft of two radios from a construction site, which Zoyas allegedly showed up to investigate, and possession of gun used in the alleged impersonation. Schwartz was unable to say when Zayas, who was arrested on Wednesday, would appear in court.

In July, Zayas was given a ride home by two police officers who saw him walking down the street in uniform. He told them his car had broken down. The next day he appeared at their station at roll-call to thank them.
"People are now starting to call in with their own stories of Abram Zayas spottings," Schwartz said.
